heroData.title: Hire in Spain (No Entity)
heroData.subtitle: Convenio Colectivo
heroData.description: Hire employees in Spain compliant with local 'Convenios' without establishing a subsidiary. EOR manages the 14-payment payroll standard.

steps.title: Convenio Allocation
steps.description: Determining the correct Collective Bargaining Agreement (Convenio Colectivo) is mandatory. This sets minimum salary, holidays (22-23 workdays), and working hours.

steps.title: Pre-Contract Data
steps.description: Collect employee's DNI/NIE (Foreigner ID) and Social Security Number (NAF). If the employee lacks an SSN, the EOR must request it via the TGSS (Tesorería General).

steps.title: Contract Drafting
steps.description: Draft indefinite contract (Contract Indefinido) in Spanish. Must specify if salary is paid in 12 or 14 installments (pagas extraordinarias).

steps.title: SEPE Registration
steps.description: Register the contract with the Public State Employment Service (SEPE) within 10 days of the start date.

steps.title: Time Tracking Setup
steps.description: Set up mandatory daily working hour registration (Registro de Jornada) compliant with Royal Decree-Law 8/2019.

items.title: Permanent Establishment (PE)
items.text: Using an EOR for >18-24 months for commercial roles (Sales VP, Country Manager) creates a high risk of the Tax Agency declaring a fictional PE.

items.title: 13th & 14th Month
items.text: By default, Spanish salaries include two extra payments (Christmas and Summer). These can be 'prorated' (prorrateo) into 12 payments if the Convenio allows.

items.title: Probation Periods
items.text: Probation is not automatic. It must be written in the contract. Max 6 months for qualified technicians/graduates, 2 months for others.

faqs.question: Can I hire contractors instead of employees?
faqs.answer: Spain has strict 'False Self-Employed' (Falso Autónomo) laws. If a contractor works mainly for you, uses your equipment, and follows your schedule, they must be converted to an employee or you face heavy fines.

faqs.question: Is a medical checkup mandatory?
faqs.answer: The employer must offer a medical checkup (Vigilancia de la Salud), but the employee can refuse it in writing unless the role involves specific hazards.

faqs.question: How does termination work?
faqs.answer: Dismissal without cause (Unfair Dismissal) is expensive in Spain: 33 days of salary per year worked (capped at 24 months). Objective dismissal (economic reasons) is 20 days/year.

items.title: Convenio Colectivo
items.text: Collective Bargaining Agreement. Determines minimum wage, hours, and holidays for a sector/region.

items.title: Falso Autónomo
items.text: False Self-Employed. Illegal practice of hiring a contractor who acts like an employee.

items.title: Finiquito
items.text: Settlement payment upon termination. Includes pro-rated bonuses and unused holidays.

steps.title: Incident Reporting
steps.description: Cut-off date (usually 20th-25th). Report 'Bajas' (Sick leave), overtime, and variable bonuses.

steps.title: Social Security Calculation
steps.description: Apply 2025 contribution rates. The maximum monthly contribution base is capped at €4,909.50 (2025 Order).

steps.title: Draft Review
steps.description: Verify Payslips (Nóminas). Ensure MEI (0.8% total) and correct IRPF retention % based on family situation (Modelo 145).

steps.title: Filings & Payment
steps.description: Submit RLC/RNT (formerly TC1/TC2) via SILTRA system. Pay employees.

items.title: Up to €12,450
items.text: 19% Rate
24% Rate
30% Rate
37% Rate

items.title: Over €60,000
items.text: 45% Rate (Typical max, regional variations up to 47%)

items.title: Beckham Law (Expat Regime)
items.text: Flat 24% tax rate on Spanish income up to €600,000 for 6 years. Must apply within 6 months of arrival. Eligibility: Moved to Spain for work, not resident in past 5 years.

items.title: Severance Taxation
items.text: Statutory severance payments (Indemnización) for unfair dismissal are tax-exempt up to €180,000.

items.title: SMI 2025
items.text: Ensure no employee is paid below the Salario Mínimo Interprofesional (updated annually, approx €1,134/month in 14 payments for 2024/25).

faqs.question: What is the CRA file?
faqs.answer: Conceptos Retributivos Abonados. A mandatory monthly file sent to TGSS detailing all payments.

faqs.question: When must payroll be paid?
faqs.answer: Typically by the last day of the month. Social Security (Seguros Sociales) is paid the following month (e.g., January contributions paid end to February).

steps.title: Unpaid Wages
steps.description: Salary corresponds to days worked in the current month up to the termination date.

steps.title: Accrued Vacation
steps.description: Unused holidays must be paid out. Calculation: (Annual Salary / 365) * Unused Days.

steps.title: Extra Payments
steps.description: Proportional part of Christmas/Summer bonuses (Pagas Extras) if they are not prorated monthly.

steps.title: Severance (Indemnización)
steps.description: The compensation for dismissal, calculated based on seniority and type of dismissal.

items.title: Daily Salary Base
items.text: Compensation is calculated on the GROSS daily salary, including the prorated part of extra payments.

items.title: Taxation
items.text: Mandatory severance (up to the statutory limit) is TAX-FREE (max €180,000). The 'Finiquito' (vacation/salary) is fully taxed.

items.title: Pre-Notice (Preaviso)
items.text: Employer must usually give 15 days notice for objective dismissal. Failure to do so requires paying those days in the Finiquito.

faqs.question: What if the employee sues?
faqs.answer: If a judge declares an Objective Dismissal as Unfair, you must pay the difference (from 20 days to 33 days/year).

faqs.question: Does seniority affect the cap?
faqs.answer: Yes. Contracts signed before Feb 2012 have higher rights (45 days/year for the period before 2012), capped at 42 months.

faqs.question: What is the FOGASA limit?
faqs.answer: FOGASA covers unpaid wages/indemnity if the employer is insolvent, capped at 2x the daily Minimum Wage (SMI). For 2025, the daily SMI is approx €46.

items.title: Finiquito
items.text: Proposed settlement document listing all amounts owed (salary, vacation, bonuses).

items.title: Carta de Despido
items.text: Formal termination letter stating the cause and effective date. Mandatory.

items.title: FOGASA
items.text: Wage Guarantee Fund that covers compensation in case of employer insolvency.

heroData.title: Set up an S.L.
heroData.subtitle: Ley Crea y Crece
heroData.description: Incorporate a Sociedad Limitada (S.L.) digitally in 7-10 days. Minimum capital now €1 under new laws.

steps.title: Name Reservation
steps.description: Request 'Certificado negativo de denominación social' from the Central Commercial Registry (RMC). Takes 24-48 hours.

steps.title: Bank Account & Capital
steps.description: Open a business bank account. Deposit min €3,000 (standard) OR €1 (under Ley Crea y Crece with liability conditions). Get the bank certificate.

steps.title: Provisional NIF
steps.description: Obtain Provisional Tax ID (NIF) from the Tax Agency (AEAT).

steps.title: Notary Signing
steps.description: Shareholders sign the Public Deed of Incorporation (Escritura) before a Spanish Notary. Remote signing is possible with Power of Attorney.

steps.title: Final Registry
steps.description: Deed is filed with the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil). Once approved, you receive the Definite NIF.

items.title: Administrator Liability
items.text: If creating an S.L. with €1 capital, shareholders are personally liable for the difference up to €3,000 until reserves cover it.

items.title: Fiscal Address
items.text: You need a registered office (Domicilio Social) in Spain. A virtual office is sufficient for the registry but you may need a physical space for substance.

items.title: Digital Certificate
items.text: Immediately apply for the FNMT Digital Certificate (Certificado Digital) for the company. Essential for all dealings with Hacienda and Social Security.

faqs.question: Do I need a resident director?
faqs.answer: No. Directors (Administradores) can be foreigners and non-residents. However, they must have a NIE (Foreigner ID) number.

faqs.question: What is the difference between S.L. and S.A.?
faqs.answer: S.L. (Limited Liability) is for small/medium business (min €3k capital). S.A. (Public Limited) is for large corps (min €60k capital, stricter auditing).

faqs.question: How long does VAT registration take?
faqs.answer: Obtaining a VIES (Intra-community VAT) number can take weeks or months and often triggers a physical inspection by the tax office to prove substance.

items.title: NIE
items.text: Número de Identidad de Extranjero. Mandatory for all foreign directors/shareholders.

items.title: Certificado Digital
items.text: Essential for online dealings with AEAT/TGSS. Get it immediately after incorporation.

items.title: Model 036
items.text: Tax census declaration form to register activity start date and tax obligations.

heroData.title: Recruitment
heroData.subtitle: Tech Hubs
heroData.description: Major hubs in Barcelona and Madrid. Malaga is emerging as a tech hub.

steps.title: Sourcing Channels
steps.description: InfoJobs (local leader) and LinkedIn (international/tech) are the primary portals. For tech talent, 'Circular' is also popular.

steps.title: GDPR Compliance
steps.description: Ensure candidates sign a data processing clause before collecting CVs. Generally illegal to ask for criminal records.

steps.title: Background Checks
steps.description: Strictly limited. Financial solvency checks only allowed for specific finance roles with consent.

steps.title: Contract Offer
steps.description: Must be written. 'Contrato Indefinido' is the norm. Probation period must be explicitly stated.

items.title: Criminal Records
items.text: Requesting 'Antecedentes Penales' is generally illegal for private employers in Spain, violating the LOPDGDD.

items.title: English Proficiency
items.text: English levels in Spain are improving but still lag behind Northern Europe. Testing language skills during interview is crucial.

items.title: Benefits
items.text: Meal vouchers (Ticket Restaurante) and Private Health Insurance (Seguro Médico) are the most valued perks.

faqs.question: Are non-competes enforceable?
faqs.answer: Yes, but they must be paid (compensación adecuada) and limited in time (max 2 years for technicians) and geography.

faqs.question: Can I hire freelancers?
faqs.answer: Yes, 'Autónomos'. But beware of 'Falso Autónomo' risk if they work exclusively for you and follow your directions.

items.title: InfoJobs
items.text: Dominant local job board for generalist roles.

items.title: LinkedIn
items.text: Essential for white-collar, tech, and international roles.

items.title: Malt
items.text: Leading platform for finding high-quality freelance talent.

heroData.title: HR Software
heroData.subtitle: Mandatory Time Tracking
heroData.description: Tools like Factorial, Personio, Sesame are popular for compliance with time tracking laws.

steps.title: Mandatory Requirement
steps.description: Since 2019, ALL companies must track start/end times for ALL employees to calculate overtime.

steps.title: Digital System
steps.description: Implement a system (Factorial, Sesame) that prevents manipulation. Paper sheets are risky.

steps.title: Employee Access
steps.description: Employees must have access to their records. Unions/Reps also have right to view monthly summaries.

steps.title: Data Retention
steps.description: Records must be kept for 4 years physically or digitally available for inspection.

items.title: Fines up to €7,500
items.text: Lack of time tracking is a serious offense. Fines range from €751 to €7,500 depending on severity and number of employees.

items.title: Digital Disconnection
items.text: Companies must have a protocol ensuring employees are not required to answer communications outside work hours.

items.title: Holiday Tracking
items.text: Spain has 14 public holidays (12 national/regional + 2 local). Validating local holidays in the HRIS is a common pain point.

faqs.question: Is biometric data allowed?
faqs.answer: Yes, but strictly regulated by GDPR. A Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) is mandatory before implementation.

faqs.question: Can I track location?
faqs.answer: Only during working hours and with prior notice. Continual tracking of company vehicles/phones outside hours is illegal.

faqs.question: What are the rules for Digital Disconnection?
faqs.answer: Under Article 88 of Law 3/2018, employers must have a protocol limiting work communications outside hours. Fines for serious infringements range from €751 to €7,500.

items.title: Factorial
items.text: Spanish unicorn, very popular for SMBs. All-in-one HR + Time Tracking.

items.title: Sesame HR
items.text: Specialized in Time Tracking and shift management. Great for blue-collar/shift work.

items.title: PayFit
items.text: Automated payroll focus, integrates with time tracking. Good for startups.

heroData.title: Gestoria
heroData.subtitle: Monthly Filing
heroData.description: Small companies use a 'Gestoria' for bookkeeping, tax (IVA/IS), and payroll.

steps.title: Invoice Collection
steps.description: Gather all issued and received invoices. Spain requires strict numbering sequences.

steps.title: Gestoria Handoff
steps.description: Send documents to Gestoria by the 20th-25th. They prepare draft tax filings.

steps.title: Quarterly Tax Filing
steps.description: Submit VAT (Modelo 303) and Withholdings (Modelo 111, 115) every Jan, Apr, Jul, Oct.

steps.title: Validating Books
steps.description: Formalizing the 'Libros Contables' in the Mercantile Registry annually by April 30th.

items.title: Mandatory Audit
items.text: Required if 2 of 3 met for 2 years: Assets > €2.85M, Turnover > €5.7M, Employees > 50.

items.title: Electronic Invoicing
items.text: B2B electronic invoicing ('Ley Crea y Crece') will become mandatory (phased 2024-2026). Ensure software represents facts.

items.title: VAT Refund
items.text: If you are in a continuous VAT credit position, apply for 'REDEME' (Monthly Refund Register) to get cash back monthly instead of annually.

faqs.question: Can I use QuickBooks/Xero?
faqs.answer: Careful. While great, they must be adapted for Spanish 'Modelo' filings. Local accountants prefer Holded, A3, or Sage.

faqs.question: What happens if I miss a filing?
faqs.answer: Automatic surcharge (recargo) of 1% + 1% per month of delay. Interest applies after 12 months.

faqs.question: When is a financial audit mandatory?
faqs.answer: If for two consecutive years, two of three limits are met: Assets > €2.85M, Turnover > €5.7M, or >50 Employees.

items.title: Modelo 303
items.text: Quarterly VAT (IVA) return. Must be filed even if zero activity.

items.title: Modelo 111
items.text: Quarterly withholding tax on employees and professionals (IRPF).

items.title: Modelo 200
items.text: Annual Corporate Tax return (Impuesto de Sociedades), filed in July.

steps.title: Prevention of Occupational Risks (PRL)
steps.description: Mandatory for all companies (even 1 employee). Must cover Risk Assessment, Health Checks, and Training. Typically outsourced to an SPA.

steps.title: Time Tracking (Registro Jornada)
steps.description: Daily recording of start/end times is mandatory for ALL employees. Records must be kept 4 years. Heavy fines for non-compliance.

steps.title: Protocolo de Acoso
steps.description: Sexual and Gender Harassment Protocol is mandatory for ALL companies. Must include a complaint channel and strict confidentiality.

steps.title: Equality Plan (>50 Staff)
steps.description: Companies with 50+ employees must register an Equality Plan (Plan de Igualdad) and a Remuneration Audit in 'REGCON'.

steps.title: Whistleblowing Channel (>50 Staff)
steps.description: Mandatory internal channel (Canal de Denuncias) for reporting regulatory breaches, anonymity guaranteed (Law 2/2023).

items.title: Digital Disconnection
items.text: Employees have the legal right not to answer emails/calls outside working hours. A policy defining this is mandatory.

items.title: Remote Work Agreement
items.text: If remote work >30% of hours, a formal 'Acuerdo de Trabajo a Distancia' must be signed and expenses (internet, equipment) compensated.

items.title: LGTBI Protocol
items.text: New since 2024: Plan for LGTBI rights and non-discrimination measures is required for companies >50 employees.

faqs.question: Do I need a DPO?
faqs.answer: A Data Protection Officer is mandatory for large scale data processing, security companies, insurers, etc. Recommended for all to ensure GDPR compliance.

faqs.question: Are health checks mandatory?
faqs.answer: The employer MUST offer them. The employee can refuse (waiver), unless the job has specific risks involving third-party safety.

faqs.question: Who must have a Whistleblowing Channel?
faqs.answer: Under Law 2/2023, all companies with 50+ employees must implement an internal reporting system that guarantees anonymity. Strict deadlines applied from Dec 2023.

items.title: AEPD
items.text: Agencia Española de Protección de Datos (Data Watchdog).

items.title: LISOS
items.text: Law on Infractions and Sanctions in the Social Order (The 'menu' of fines).

items.title: PRL
items.text: Prevención de Riesgos Laborales (Occupational Safety).

steps.title: Quarterly VAT (Modelo 303)
steps.description: Filed every April 20, July 20, October 20, and January 30. Large companies (SII) file monthly.

steps.title: Corporate Tax Payment (Modelo 202)
steps.description: Advance payments on account of CIT are due in April, October, and December (dates vary, typically 20th).

steps.title: Annual CIT Return (Modelo 200)
steps.description: The definitive annual return is due 25 calendar days after the 6-month period following the fiscal year end (July 25th for calendar FY).

steps.title: Annual Accounts Deposit
steps.description: Statutory financial statements must be deposited with the Mercantile Registry by July 30th (for calendar FY).

steps.title: Informative Returns (Modelo 347)
steps.description: February 28th deadline to declare operations with third parties exceeding €3,005.06 annually.

rows.label: Dividend Withholding
values: EU residents exempt subject to conditions

items.title: Patent Box Regime
items.text: Up to 60% reduction in the tax base for income derived from licensing patents, software, and industrial designs. One of the most aggressive in the EU.

items.title: R&D Tax Credit
items.text: 25% deduction on R&D expenses (plus 42% on excess over average of prior 2 years). Plus 12% for IT innovation (i.e., software development).

items.title: Transfer Pricing
items.text: Related-party transactions must be at arm's length. Master File and Local File documentation mandatory for criteria. Strict audit focus.

faqs.question: Are startup stock options taxed?
faqs.answer: Under the 'Ley de Startups', up to €50,000 of stock options per year are exempt from income tax until exercised or after 10 years.

faqs.question: What is the Beckham Law?
faqs.answer: A special expat regime allowing new residents to pay a flat 24% tax on Spanish income (up to €600k) for 6 years, shielding foreign assets/income.

faqs.question: Can I reclaim VAT?
faqs.answer: Yes. Input VAT is deductible against output VAT. If input > output, you can request a refund (monthly for REDEME register, annual otherwise).

items.title: Modelo 200
items.text: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return.

items.title: Modelo 303
items.text: Quarterly/Monthly VAT Return.

items.title: Modelo 111
items.text: Quarterly Withholding verification (Employees/Professionals).

items.title: Modelo 390
items.text: Annual VAT Summary Recap.

heroData.title: B2B Contracts
heroData.subtitle: Comm. Code
heroData.description: Spanish B2B contracts are governed by the Commercial Code. The 'Ley Crea y Crece' imposes strict 60-day payment limits.

steps.title: Identify Parties
steps.description: Verify the NIF (Tax ID) and the power of attorney (Poderes) of the signers via the Mercantile Registry.

steps.title: Payment Terms
steps.description: MUST be under 60 days from invoice date. Clauses stating '90 days' or '120 days' are null and void by law.

steps.title: Tacit Renewal (Tácita Reconducción)
steps.description: Contracts renew automatically by default (Civil Code Art 1566) unless a specific 'Notice of Non-Renewal' clause is included.

steps.title: Data Processing
steps.description: If the vendor accesses personal data, a DPA (Data Processing Agreement) annex is mandatory under GDPR.

steps.title: Jurisdiction (Fuero)
steps.description: Explicitly state the courts (e.g., 'Courts of Madrid') to avoid ambiguity. Arbitration is a faster, pricier alternative.

items.title: Tacit Renewal
items.text: Essential to disable 'Tácita Reconducción' explicitly if you do not want the contract to auto-renew for another full term.

items.title: Electronic Signatures
items.text: Qualified Digital Signatures (e.g., FNMT, DNIe) or Advanced signatures (DocuSign, Signaturit) are fully valid (Law 6/2020).

items.title: Bilingual Contracts
items.text: Prevailing language clause is vital. In Spanish courts, the Spanish version will always be the reference.

faqs.question: Can I use UK/US Law?
faqs.answer: For B2B contracts, yes (Rome I Regulation). However, mandatory Spanish 'public order' rules (payment terms, fraud) still apply.

faqs.question: Is email legally binding?
faqs.answer: Yes, if authenticity can be proven. However, for contract amendments or termination notices, 'Burofax' (certified fax/mail) is recommended for proof of delivery.

faqs.question: Which court jurisdiction should I choose?
faqs.answer: Spanish courts uphold 'hybrid' clauses. Agencies often prefer explicit submission to the Courts of Barcelona or Madrid, or arbitration to avoid regional court delays.

items.title: Burofax
items.text: Certified communication service used in Spain to prove content and delivery date legally.

items.title: Poderes Notariales
items.text: Notarized Power of Attorney proving the signatory has authority to bind the company.

items.title: Objeto Social
items.text: The corporate purpose defined in the bylaws; contracts outside this may be voidable.

heroData.title: Software Development
heroData.subtitle: Hubs & Talent
heroData.description: Spain is a top European tech hub (Madrid, Barcelona, Malaga). High-quality talent at competitive rates vs Northern Europe.

steps.title: Choose Model
steps.description: Decide between hiring local employees (employer costs ~30%), B2B Contractors (Autónomos), or an Employer of Record (EOR).

steps.title: IP Assignment
steps.description: Critical for contractors: 'Work for Hire' is NOT automatic. You MUST have a written IP transfer clause (Cesión de Derechos).

steps.title: Equipment (Remote)
steps.description: By law (Remote Work Law), companies must provide equipment (laptop, etc.) and cover expenses for remote staff.

steps.title: Recruitment Channels
steps.description: Post on specialized boards like Manfred (GetManfred) or Tecnoempleo for best local reach.

steps.title: Onboarding
steps.description: Register employees with Social Security BEFORE their first day. Late registration equals huge fines.

items.title: Malaga Valley
items.text: Rapidly growing hub (Google Safety Center). Lower cost of living than Madrid/BCN, high quality of life, attracting senior expats.

items.title: Non-EU Talent
items.text: The 'Highly Qualified Professional' (HQP) visa allows fast-track hiring of non-EU devs. No labor market test required.

items.title: Stock Options
items.text: Taxable as income upon exercise unless under strict 'Ley de Startups' exemption (up to €50k/year exempt).

faqs.question: Does the company own the code?
faqs.answer: For Employees: Yes, presumed by law unless agreed otherwise. For Contractors: NO, unless explicitly assigned in writing.

faqs.question: English proficiency?
faqs.answer: High in senior roles and startups. Mixed in junior/legacy corporate pools. Coding tests in English are standard practice.

faqs.question: Are remote work expenses mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Remote Work Law (Royal Decree-Law 28/2020) requires a written agreement and compensation for expenses (internet, equipment) if remote work > 30%.

items.title: Manfred
items.text: Community-driven, high-quality tech talent pool, agent-based model.

items.title: Tecnoempleo
items.text: Traditional IT job board with high volume of candidates.

items.title: LinkedIn
items.text: Essential for mid-to-senior roles. Use 'Hiring' filters.

heroData.title: Digital Growth
heroData.subtitle: SEO & Performance
heroData.description: Spanish agencies offer high-quality creative and performance marketing at costs 30-40% lower than UK/US.

steps.title: Project Based
steps.description: Fixed price for website launches, branding kits, or specific campaigns. 50% upfront, 50% on delivery.

steps.title: Monthly Retainer
steps.description: Common for SEO, Social Media, and PPC management. Usually essentially 6-12 month contracts.

steps.title: Performance (CPA)
steps.description: Some aggressive agencies work on a Commission/CPA basis, though they usually require a minimum setup fee.

items.title: Localization is Key
items.text: Do not just translate. Spanish consumers value 'Cercanía' (closeness). Tone should be warm but professional. Avoid Latin American Spanish terms.

items.title: Regional Languages
items.text: In Catalonia, Basque Country, and Galicia, using the local language (Catalan, Euskera, Galician) in ads can significantly boost conversion.

items.title: WhatsApp Marketing
items.text: WhatsApp is ubiquitous in Spain (used by 90%+). Agencies often use WhatsApp Business API for customer service and leads.

faqs.question: What are the main ad platforms?
faqs.answer: Google Ads and Meta (Instagram/Facebook) dominate. TikTok is growing fast for Gen Z. LinkedIn is essential for B2B.

faqs.question: Is influencer marketing regulated?
faqs.answer: Yes. The 'Influencer Law' (2024) requires influencers to clearly label sponsored content, similar to TV ads.

faqs.question: Does the Digital Services Tax affect agencies?
faqs.answer: Directly, only if global turnover > €750M. However, agencies often see the 3% tax passed on by platforms (Google, Meta) in their ad invoices.

items.title: IAB Spain
items.text: The main association for digital advertising, setting standards and publishing key market reports.

items.title: Club de Creativos (c de c)
items.text: Prestigious organization promoting creative excellence in Spanish advertising.

items.title: Agencias de España
items.text: Association representing independent Spanish private capital agencies.
